verdictStatement: Every finding from both v14 lanes is repaired, and I tested substance rather than presence, which is the discipline my v13 ACCEPT lacked. The claude2v13 pin now enumerates the frozen file's advisory ADV-1 — confirmed through an unchanged digest rather than a read this prompt does not authorise — and the false 'no additional v13 Claude findings' clause is replaced by a sentence that records the advisory, explains the 0/0 shorthand, and timestamps its own amendment. The trailing duplicate guidance line is deleted and no fresh copy appended. CLAUDE-V13-ADV-1 is booked not-folded with the pin obligation and the unresolved substance correctly separated. Codex's SARIFV14-A1 is folded by removing the stale canonicalized sentence. My CLAUDE-V14-ADV-2 is booked not-folded with an accurate description. Beyond the repairs, v15 tightens its own rules unprompted: it now states that succession metadata does not authorize unrostered remeasurement-block edits, and that the prior LIVE block is rostered whenever a new one is added — and both hold in this diff. Most importantly for me, I applied the check I said at v14 should be standing and diffed both new pins field-for-field against the frozen files rather than parsing them, because a sweep cannot see an omitted roster. Six arrays, six exact matches, including both of my advisories. I also chased the seven copies of the shorter SATISFIED reminder and found them to be per-generation block terminators from a convention that ended at v9, constant since v10 and untouched here — not the defect I faulted at v14. The contract's substance is byte-identical to v14 throughout. One minor advisory remains, on three pre-convention remeasurement blocks, and it does not block.

coordinatorNote: ACCEPT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-122 stays OPEN at file 08 line 304; nothing here marks any DR SATISFIED, authorizes implementation, resurrects G17, mints a D9 or DR-006 recipe, or creates anything under D-096 (A). I rejected v14 and accept v15, so the basis should be visible: all four of my v14 items and both Codex v14 items are repaired, each verified against bytes, and the projection contract itself has not moved. Three things worth carrying. First, I applied the structural remedy I recommended at v14 — diffing each new pin's roster field-for-field against the frozen file it names, rather than relying on the accounting sweep, which by construction cannot see an omitted roster. Both new pins pass. If one rule survives this lineage, make it that one; note that reviewGuidance already carried 'Attack a pin that omits the pinned file's advisory roster' at index 49 and the defect still occurred twice, so the check needs to be performed, not merely listed. Second, v15 tightened two rules on itself that nobody asked for, about unrostered remeasurement edits and about rostering the block being demoted, and both hold in the diff; that is the kind of change worth preserving in any successor. Third, my one advisory concerns three pre-convention remeasurement blocks and is genuinely minor — I would not spend a round on it. Given my v13 ACCEPT proved too generous, I will say plainly what is different here: at v13 I confirmed that repairs were present; here I diffed rosters against their sources, re-derived the verbatim layer from live bytes, and ran down a seven-fold duplication that turned out to be innocent. The remaining risk I cannot retire is scope: this prompt names only the v14 verdicts, so pins from earlier generations were digest-verified but not roster-diffed.
